body:
## Summary

Enable the simpler runtime support needed by `pl.prefetch.async_prefetch` in **a2a3 onboard kernel mode**, for both **TMR** (`tensormap_and_ringbuffer`) and **HBG** (`host_build_graph`). Previously, `Worker` rejected kernel mode with `enable_sdma=True`, and the kernel context did not provision the SDMA workspace needed by `TPREFETCH_ASYNC`.

This PR targets **`feat/kernel-mode-integration-test`**, based on `17e342455`, and combines the TMR and HBG implementations in one commit.

```python
worker = Worker(
    level=2,
    platform="a2a3",
    runtime="host_build_graph",  # or "tensormap_and_ringbuffer"
    execution_mode="kernel",
    device_id=device_id,
    enable_sdma=True,
)
```

## Implementation

- Carry `enable_sdma` and the optional warmup binary through Worker, ChipWorker and the native kernel-init ABI. Provision and warm SDMA during initialization, outside capture, using the context's hidden AICore stream.
- Snapshot workspace addresses into each Runtime instead of relying on shared AICPU globals during dispatch. TMR carries the snapshot in its device descriptor; HBG initializes both per-core dispatch payload buffers and exposes `get_dma_workspace(args, kind)`.
- Reuse the workspace during eager execution and ACLGraph replay. Disabled contexts publish zero addresses; unsupported targets reject SDMA before resource acquisition. Workspace teardown follows the context lifetime; the caller retains ownership of the device.
- Add missing HBG header dependencies to the onboard AICore build commands. This prevents a stale binary from retaining an incompatible Runtime/context layout after incremental builds.

The native `simpler_kernel_mode_init` signature changes; rebuild the bindings and runtime libraries together.

## Onboard test data and results

Each runtime has five new cases: eager, first-use capture/replay, context recreation, disabled workspace, and program/kernel workspace isolation. Each case uses **100 rounds with 128 FP32 elements**; round `r` supplies `r * 257 + i`, and output is reset to `-999` before execution. The real kernel executes `TPREFETCH_ASYNC` and waits for its event before copying. HBG runs **two dependent tasks through a runtime-owned intermediate tensor**. Output is checked for exact equality; disabled-workspace cases retain the sentinel.

The native observer checks stable resident launch argument addresses, **zero invocation `rtMalloc` calls**, and **zero internal invocation synchronization**. The replay case captures the first invocation without eager priming.

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New TMR prefetch cases | 5 passed |
| New HBG prefetch cases | 5 passed |
| Isolated single-device SDMA sweep, including both runtimes, program prefetch and bounded fault teardown | 12 passed |
| Existing HBG capture/replay suite | 20 passed |
| Existing TMR capture regression (`cold_unsynced`, `fresh_inputs`, `eager_batch`, `eager_dag`) | 4 passed, 100 rounds each |
| HBG onboard L2, isolated by runtime | 41 passed, 1 skipped |
| TMR onboard L2, isolated by runtime | 58 passed |
| HBG/kernel C++ targets | 66 passed |
| Python unit tests | 2560 passed, 73 skipped |
| a2a3sim L2 | 42 passed, 8 skipped |
| Available runtime builds | Passed |
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks (including clang-tidy and pyright) | Passed |

## Boundaries and broader regression findings

- PyPTO DSL integration additionally requires the companion compiler patch linked below; the runtime-only tests do not establish frontend correctness by themselves.
- Kernel SDMA remains unsupported on A5, simulation and provider-disabled builds. Multi-device onboard SDMA is not covered.
- A combined `--level 2` invocation without a runtime filter bypassed process isolation and reported 94 passed, 1 skipped and 5 failures at HBG/TMR transitions. A clean, unmodified baseline reproduced the same failure (two HBG scenes passed, then the first TMR scene failed with AICPU status 507018); all three passed with dispatcher isolation. This matches the existing onboard constraint: one runtime per device per process. The complete runtime-isolated sweeps above pass.
- The initial broader C++ run had 179 passing targets and two failing pre-window cancellation targets; both failures also reproduce on the unmodified baseline. The broader simulation resource sweep timed out in `TestAllreduceIbingRejectNonSum`; its baseline behavior is not established. These broader runs are not claimed as fully passing.

Implementation details, reproduction commands and retained local log locations are in [the validation report](https://github.com/TaoZQY/simpler/blob/codex/tmr-kernel-prefetch/docs/kernel-integration-validation.md#tmr-and-hbg-kernel-mode-async-prefetch).

## Full MIX integration fixes

Full 24-AIC/48-AIV MIX execution exposed shared SDMA channels, untracked UB scratch, and completion polling that was too frequent under full AIV fan-out.

This PR assigns a unique channel to each resident AIV (`core_id - aic_count`), propagates it through both dispatch payloads and cold initialization, and exposes it to generated kernels. The compiler include path now also exposes the architecture platform constants, including the system-counter frequency.

[The companion PyPTO fix](https://github.com/YunjiQin/pypto/pull/1), targeting #3001's source branch, reserves 256 bytes of UB per context in both memory planners and lowers `pl.prefetch.wait` to a local adapter. The adapter uses the existing public `AsyncEvent::Test()` with approximately 1 microsecond between incomplete probes and a 20 ms event deadline. Timeout still returns false and does not cancel outstanding work.

**PTO-ISA is unchanged.** The pin remains the integration base's `327cd5869f3a7c4d2c6a1b945b2aed06e7665c5d`. PTO-ISA #363 is not a prerequisite. The earlier same-binary, same-deadline experiment supports pacing; it does not require that policy to live in the generic library. Native SDMA Wait and submission-internal waits retain their original behavior.

Validation using the original, clean PTO-ISA checkout, after rebuilding both runtime libraries, the binding and torch adapter:
- **16/16 onboard cases passed**, 100 changing-input rounds each, 336.52 seconds. Includes the 65-post flag-slot reuse boundary on both runtimes in eager and replay.
- Three additional fresh-process TMR replay stress runs passed, **300 rounds each**.
- 147 focused PyPTO CPU regressions and 20 Simpler compiler-path tests passed, including deterministic wait-policy checks.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed.


Onboard environment: A3, CANN 9.0.0, torch 2.6.0 / torch_npu 2.6.0.post2. CANN 9.2 / torch_npu 2.10 and A5 onboard validation are not claimed. [Investigation](https://github.com/TaoZQY/simpler/blob/codex/tmr-kernel-prefetch/docs/investigations/2026-10-sdma-wait-probe-results.md) preserves earlier failures and the choice to scope the workaround to PyPTO.

The docs workflow still fails at `Highlight.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'md'`, reproduced on earlier unchanged PR heads and separate from these fixes.
title: Add: support kernel-mode async prefetch for TMR and HBG
